questions.q: How does capacity planning differ from Lesson 55's right-sizing?
options: Right-sizing reactively asks if today's SKU fits today's measured load; capacity planning forward-looks at what load will be in the future
They are the exact same process performed at different times of year
Capacity planning only applies to Azure resources, never Fabric Capacities
Right-sizing is forward-looking and capacity planning is reactive
questions.explain: Right-sizing keeps the present correct; capacity planning keeps the future from arriving as a surprise.

questions.q: Why is temporarily overprovisioning for one known peak night (like New Year's Eve) cheaper than sizing the whole year around it?
options: Paying for a larger SKU for one night is far cheaper than maintaining that larger baseline capacity for the entire year
There's no actual cost difference between the two approaches
Peak events never actually require any extra capacity
Sizing for the whole year is always the cheaper option regardless of event frequency
questions.explain: A sudden, temporary, foreseeable event is a different planning shape than gradual, predictable growth.

questions.q: Why does a 90-day trend view reveal something a single day's utilization snapshot doesn't?
options: It shows whether consumption is flat, growing steadily, or accelerating — direction that a single-day number can't reveal
A single day's snapshot always shows more information than a trend
Trend views and snapshots always show identical information
90-day trends are only useful for cost management, not capacity planning
questions.explain: A steadily climbing trend signals it's time to plan the next SKU increase on your own schedule, before sustained bursting forces the decision.

questions.q: How does capacity planning connect back to Lesson 54's cost management?
options: Planning ahead makes the cost of growth a deliberate, budgeted decision in advance, rather than a surprise bill after a reactive SKU bump under pressure
The two topics are completely unrelated
Capacity planning replaces the need for any cost management at all
Cost management only applies to retention policies, not capacity
questions.explain: The forecast from capacity planning is meant to be the input Lesson 54's cost conversation is actually built around.

questions.q: What does gradual growth planning typically involve, compared to peak-event planning?
options: Projecting a trend forward and adjusting the baseline SKU before the trend catches up with it, rather than temporary deliberate overprovisioning
Exactly the same approach as planning for a single known peak night
Growth planning never actually requires any SKU adjustment
Peak-event planning always requires permanently raising the baseline SKU
questions.explain: Growth is addressed with a baseline adjustment ahead of the trend; a peak event is addressed with temporary overprovisioning instead.
